subject: special-education
intro: Special education leads to the professionals who individualise learning: licensed special education teachers in every school band, plus the speech and occupational therapists who support students' communication and independence.

roles.title: Special Education Teachers, Elementary School
roles.what: Teach elementary school students with disabilities, adapting general lessons to individual needs, writing and following IEPs, and working closely with families and support specialists so every learner can access the curriculum.
roles.where: The foundations unit — IDEA, the IEP process, high-incidence disabilities — and the evidence-based instruction unit's explicit instruction and positive behaviour support are the daily toolkit of the elementary special education classroom.

roles.title: Special Education Teachers, Secondary School
roles.what: Teach secondary students with disabilities, adapt subject content to individual education plans, monitor progress toward goals, and coordinate the transition services that prepare older students for work and adult life.
roles.where: Assessment and progress monitoring, data-based individualisation, and the collaboration and transition unit — working with families and transition to adulthood — map directly onto the secondary special educator's job.

roles.title: Speech-Language Pathologists
roles.what: Assess and treat people with speech, language, voice and fluency disorders, select and teach alternative communication systems, and work with children whose communication needs shape how they learn.
roles.where: The learner development unit's low-incidence and sensory disabilities topic covers the communication profiles SLPs work with, and progress monitoring gives you the data habits their therapy plans run on.

roles.title: Occupational Therapists
roles.what: Assess, plan and organise rehabilitative programmes that build daily living and independence skills for people with disabilities or developmental delays, adapting environments and modifying tasks that present barriers.
roles.where: Universal design for learning and the low-incidence disabilities topics teach how environments and tasks can be adapted — the same logic OTs apply when engineering independence for students with disabilities.
